title: Can three threes make zero, two, four, six, nine and twelve?
description: Three threes are joined with the four operations and brackets to make zero, two, four, six, nine and twelve. Brackets change the order of working. Keeko doubts that three threes can only be added together.
teaching_notes: One idea: any of the four operations can join three threes, and brackets set the order of working. Watch for students who only add the threes.

source: Using three 3s, the four operations and brackets, find expressions for 0, 2, 4, 6, 9 and 12.
video_script.why: A learner joins three equal numbers with the four operations and brackets to reach different values.
video_script.substitution: Replace the three threes with three of any other number and try to reach other values.
video_script.anchor: three cards each showing three, with the four operations and a pair of brackets beside them
video_script.wrong_answer: three threes can only be added together
video_script.wrong_move: joins the three 3s only with plus, so 3 + 3 + 3 = 9 is the only value found
video_script.payoff_line: All six numbers can be made from three threes.

final_answer.spoken: all six numbers can be made from three threes

maths_rules: the slip: only adding gives 9 and nothing else
video_script.design: Three cards of three sit on the left, with the four operation signs and brackets on the right. For each target, the cards are joined with signs and brackets and the value appears.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; three cards each showing 3, the signs + − × ÷, a pair of brackets, and the targets 0, 2, 4, 6, 9, 12

marks.h3: the six targets appear and glow

narration: <bookmark mark='h1'/>This is a puzzle from your book about three threes.
<bookmark mark='h2'/>We may use the four operations and brackets to join them.
<bookmark mark='h3'/>Can we make zero, two, four, six, nine and twelve?

beats.on_screen: the three cards and the six targets stay on the board and the targets keep glowing

marks.t1: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='t1'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 3 + 3 ÷ 3 with the division circled first; (3 + 3) ÷ 3 with the bracket circled first

marks.g3: an arrow shows the circled part is worked out first

beats.colours: the part worked first in a second colour
narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>Without a bracket, multiplication and division are worked before addition and subtraction.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>A bracket is worked first.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>The same threes can give different values with a bracket.

beats.on_screen: Given: three 3s, the four operations and brackets; targets 0, 2, 4, 6, 9, 12

marks.gv1: the three threes, the operations and the targets are written

narration: <bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, three threes, the four operations and brackets, and six targets.

beats.on_screen: To find: an expression for each target using all three 3s

marks.fd1: the words an expression for each target are written

narration: <bookmark mark='fd1'/>We have to find an expression for each target, using all three threes.

marks.s11: 3 − 3 is put in a bracket and becomes 0
marks.s13: 3 + 3 is put in a bracket and becomes 6

narration: <bookmark mark='s11'/>Step one, make zero and two.
For zero, take three minus three inside a bracket first.
<bookmark mark='s12'/>Three times open bracket three minus three close bracket is three times zero, which is zero.
<bookmark mark='s13'/>For two, add two threes inside a bracket.
<bookmark mark='s14'/>Open bracket three plus three close bracket divided by three is six divided by three, which is two.
<bookmark mark='s21'/>Step two, make four, using three plus three divided by three with no bracket. The division comes first.
<bookmark mark='s22'/>Three divided by three is one, so the value is three plus one, which is four.
<bookmark mark='s31'/>Step three, make six and nine, and for six, three times three is nine.
<bookmark mark='s32'/>Then nine minus three is six.
<bookmark mark='s33'/>For nine, add all three threes, which is three plus three plus three.
<bookmark mark='s41'/>Step four, make twelve, and three times three is nine.
<bookmark mark='s42'/>Then nine plus three is twelve.

marks.a1: all six expressions are listed beside their targets
marks.a2: the six targets are ticked and the answer is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='a1'/>All six numbers can be made from three threes.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>Each one uses all three threes, with brackets or operations that suit it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the board
narration: <bookmark mark='k1'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: three 3s can only be added together; it is struck out and 3 × 3 − 3 lights up

marks.k2: Keeko's bubble shows three 3s can only be added
marks.k3: 3 × 3 − 3 lights up with its three threes

narration: <bookmark mark='k2'/>Keeko thinks three threes can only be added together.
<bookmark mark='k3'/>But three times three minus three also uses three threes.
<bookmark mark='k4'/>Any of the four operations can join the threes.
